definitions.explanation: A male sovereign or ruler. Used for kings in history, fairy tales, and foreign countries.
Used as a suffix or title to indicate the supreme or dominant figure in a field. Common in games, sports, and informal rankings.

examples.japanese: {王|おう}が{国|くに}を{治|おさ}めた。
むかしむかし、ある{国|くに}に{王|おう}がいました。
examples.english: Once upon a time, there was a king in a certain land.

examples.japanese: ルイ{十四世|じゅうよんせい}は「{太陽王|たいようおう}」と{呼|よ}ばれた{偉大|いだい}な{王|おう}だった。
examples.english: Louis XIV was a great king called the 'Sun King.'

examples.japanese: {本塁打|ほんるいだ}{王|おう}に{輝|かがや}いた。
examples.english: He won the home run crown.

examples.japanese: あの{店|みせ}はラーメンの{王|おう}だ。
examples.english: That shop is the king of ramen.

examples.japanese: {将棋|しょうぎ}では{王|おう}を{取|と}られたら{負|ま}けだ。
examples.english: In shogi, you lose if your king is captured.

notes:
Means 'king' both literally and figuratively. As a suffix, it designates the top figure in a domain.

COMPOUNDS:
- {王様|おうさま} — king (polite/fairy-tale form)
- {王子|おうじ} — prince
- {王女|おうじょ} — princess
- {王国|おうこく} — kingdom
- {王座|おうざ} — throne
- {女王|じょおう} — queen
- {国王|こくおう} — king (of a country)
- {王冠|おうかん} — crown

AS A SUFFIX (~{王|おう}):
- {本塁打王|ほんるいだおう} — home run king/champion
- {打点王|だてんおう} — RBI champion
- {海賊王|かいぞくおう} — pirate king
- {魔王|まおう} — demon king

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {皇帝|こうてい} — emperor (higher rank than king)
- {天皇|てんのう} — Emperor of Japan (specific title)
- {君主|くんしゅ} — monarch, sovereign (formal/generic)
